answers.children: Pharaoh Hounds can be good with children when raised together. Their graceful athleticism leads to energetic play that may overwhelm smaller children while their independent nature means they sometimes withdraw from rough handling. Owners must channel the breed's high energy and deep family loyalty into supervised interaction that respects the dog's ancient sighthound instincts. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 6/10)
answers.other-pets: Pharaoh Hounds often struggle with other pets because of their strong prey drive. Bred on Malta to chase rabbits across rugged terrain their intense instinct makes small animals a trigger for pursuit while same-sex tension can appear with unfamiliar dogs. The elegant sighthound's loyalty stays firmly with its own family rather than extending to household companions.
answers.exercise: Pharaoh Hounds need at least one hour of vigorous daily exercise. Long runs or sprinting in a secure field suit their lean muscular build and ancient role pursuing small game over Maltese scrubland. Without this outlet the independent energetic hound becomes restless and may scale fences to chase anything that moves.
answers.shedding: Yes — Pharaoh Hounds shed lightly year-round. Their short smooth single coat produces minimal loose hair that rarely collects on furniture or clothing. The sleek texture means grooming remains simple yet the elegant sighthound still requires occasional wiping to maintain its clean appearance in the home.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is truly hypoallergenic yet the Pharaoh Hound is sometimes suggested for allergy sufferers. Its short smooth coat releases little dander compared with longer or double-coated breeds. The minimal shedding from this ancient Maltese sighthound reduces airborne allergens though individual reactions still vary.
answers.training: Pharaoh Hounds prove moderately easy to train. Their intelligence allows quick learning but the independent spirit developed for hunting rabbits without constant human direction can lead to selective obedience. Consistent work that respects the breed's aloofness with strangers and playful energy yields the best results.
answers.lifespan: Pharaoh Hounds live 11-14 years. Their lean athletic build and robust health shaped by centuries adapting to Malta's harsh environment support this range. The graceful sighthound's energetic yet independent temperament helps maintain condition when provided with adequate exercise and mental outlets throughout life.
answers.size: Pharaoh Hounds reach 45-55 lb and stand 21-25 in at the shoulder. Their elegant sculpted proportions and muscular frame create a graceful presence that feels both substantial and light on its feet. Living with this medium sighthound means sharing space with an agile athlete built for speed rather than bulk.
answers.barking: Pharaoh Hounds bark moderately. The breed tends to vocalise at rustling sounds or strangers reflecting its alert yet discerning nature as a Maltese hunter. Their independent character prevents constant noise while the occasional bark serves to communicate excitement or the famous blush-induced arousal.
answers.apartment: Pharaoh Hounds can live in an apartment if given sufficient exercise. Their ability to settle indoors stems from the independent temperament that lets them rest calmly after activity yet the high energy and prey drive demand secure daily outlets to prevent destructive behaviour in confined spaces.
answers.first-time: Pharaoh Hounds are not ideal as a first dog. The strong prey drive and independent nature bred for pursuing game on Maltese terrain require an experienced handler who can manage chasing and provide the mental stimulation this intelligent sighthound demands without becoming aloof or bored.
